summary: Backend-only regression test for the iteration-15 refactor: extraction of blog/policies/pricing/discounts routers from server.py + reCAPTCHA re-enable on /leads & /contact + explicit-origin CORS for httpOnly cookie auth. Created /app/backend/tests/test_router_refactor.py (30 tests, all PASSING) covering every public + admin endpoint of the 4 new routers, full CRUD cycle with create→read→publish→public-GET→delete + view_count increment, auth enforcement (401/403 with anon client), reCAPTCHA enforcement (missing token → 400 'reCAPTCHA requis', invalid token → 400 'Échec de la vérification reCAPTCHA') for both /api/v1/leads and /api/v1/contact, CORS behavior on direct backend (localhost:8001) — allowed origin reflects ACAO + sets HttpOnly dt_access_token/dt_refresh_token cookies, disallowed origin gets no ACAO + no wildcard, preview-subdomain regex matches. Plus untouched routes (/portfolio, /services, /pricing, /admin/leads, /admin/clients, /admin/invoices, /admin/projects, /auth/me, /ai/draft-quote) still respond.
action_items: (Already fixed by testing agent) Stale tests in test_blog_pdf_portal.py (TestLeadSubmissionWithRecaptcha class) and test_murs_accent.py — they were written when reCAPTCHA was disabled and asserted 200 on POST /api/v1/leads without a token. Updated test_blog_pdf_portal.py to assert 400 + French messages; marked the 2 murs_accent lead-creation tests as @pytest.mark.skip with explicit reason (cannot obtain valid Google reCAPTCHA token in CI).

(Pre-existing, NOT a refactor regression) Other test files contain the same stale reCAPTCHA assumption and continue to fail when run from a shell that has REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL exported: test_cmgeorges_api.py (TestLeadsCRUD, TestContactForm, plus TestAuthentication/TestPublicEndpoints which look cascaded — main agent may want to investigate), test_notifications.py (test_create_lead_triggers_notification, test_mark_notification_as_read, test_delete_notification — all need a recaptcha bypass path or admin-side lead creation). Not blocking; they predate this iteration.

(Pre-existing) test_auth_reset_and_ai_drafts.py::test_forgot_password_rate_limit is flaky — got 4×200 instead of 429 on the 4th request; rate-limit window may have already elapsed or storage was reset between requests. Unrelated to this refactor.

(Pre-existing) test_cookie_auth.py and test_api_v2.py require REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL to be exported in the shell (they don't read frontend/.env). When unset they crash with 'No scheme supplied'. Consider adding the same env-fallback as I added to test_router_refactor.py.
critical_code_review_comments: Router extraction is clean: all 4 new routers follow the build_xxx_router(db, get_current_user, require_admin, create_audit_log) DI pattern; no global imports of server.py state from inside the routers; URLs preserved exactly (under v1_router prefix). Good refactor.

blog.py update_blog_post correctly handles the publish-transition: sets published_at only on first publish (checks existing.published_at). However it does NOT clear published_at if status is moved back to draft/archived — minor edge case, probably intentional (preserve history).

discounts.py uppercases the code on create AND on validate (code.upper()) — symmetric and correct. The validate-discount endpoint does NOT increment times_used on a successful validation; that is left to whatever code actually applies the discount (probably checkout/lead flow). Worth confirming no caller assumes validate increments it.

pricing.py PricingItemUpdate is missing 'service_type' — once an item is created, you cannot move it between service_type buckets via PATCH. Probably intentional; flagging in case admin UI exposes such a control.

policies.py POST sets is_active=False on ALL other policies of the same policy_type before inserting — good 'only one active per type' semantic. PATCH does NOT enforce this; if an admin manually flips is_active=true on an archived policy while another active one exists, the public endpoint /policies-public will dedupe by policy_type via dict-collision and silently keep whichever comes last from Mongo. Consider adding a uniqueness guard in PATCH.

Auth enforcement on the 4 new routers is consistent with server.py legacy: GET/POST/PATCH use Depends(get_current_user) (any authenticated user passes), DELETE uses Depends(require_admin). This matches the spec.

verify_recaptcha fix (server.py:856-890) is correct — v2 checkbox response has no 'score' field, so the previous score>=0.5 gate was over-strict. New code returns True on success and only applies the score check when a score is present (v3). Tested via real Google siteverify endpoint with invalid token → returns False → endpoint correctly returns 400 'Échec de la vérification reCAPTCHA'.

CORS allow_origins is now an explicit list (cmgeorges.ca, www.cmgeorges.ca, decotouche.com, www.decotouche.com, localhost:3000, 127.0.0.1:3000, serviceflow-preview.preview.emergentagent.com) + regex `https://.*\.preview\.emergentagent\.com$`. allow_credentials=True is now safe (no wildcard). Startup log confirms: 'CORS allow_origins: [...]' + 'CORS allow_origin_regex: https://.*\.preview\.emergentagent\.com$'.

Login on direct backend (localhost:8001) with Origin https://cmgeorges.ca returns 200 + Set-Cookie dt_access_token + dt_refresh_token both with HttpOnly + access-control-allow-origin=https://cmgeorges.ca + access-control-allow-credentials=true. Verified ✅.

Disallowed Origin https://malicious.example on OPTIONS preflight: FastAPI CORS middleware does NOT echo back an access-control-allow-origin header — verified ✅. Wildcard '*' also not present (would break credentials).

server.py is still ~5050+ lines after extracting 520 lines into the 4 routers. Still well over the 700-line guideline. Future refactors could extract: leads & contact (~400 lines), clients, invoices, projects, AI, signature flows. Not blocking.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_blog_pdf_portal.py (TestLeadSubmissionWithRecaptcha: 2 tests updated for re-enabled reCAPTCHA — now assert 400 + French messages)
/app/backend/tests/test_murs_accent.py (2 lead-creation tests marked @pytest.mark.skip with reason — cannot get valid reCAPTCHA in CI)

success_rate.backend: 100% (30/30 new router-refactor tests pass; 120/134 of the broader regression suite pass, 14 skipped; the remaining failures in test_cmgeorges_api/test_notifications/test_auth_reset are all pre-existing stale tests, NOT regressions of this iteration)

seed_data_creation: test_router_refactor.py creates and deletes its own data in the same test (full CRUD cycle): one TEST blog post (auto-deleted), one TEST warranty policy (auto-deleted), one TEST pricing item (auto-deleted), one TEST discount code (auto-deleted). No leftover seed data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable assets: /app/backend/tests/test_router_refactor.py — comprehensive coverage of the 4 new routers + reCAPTCHA + CORS + untouched routes. Uses BASE_URL with fallback to reading /app/frontend/.env (so works without env vars exported). Uses a hard-isolated `anon_client` fixture (fresh requests.Session, no cookies) to verify auth enforcement — IMPORTANT: do NOT reuse the session-scoped fixture for unauth tests because the admin_token fixture's call to /auth/login sets dt_access_token cookie on the session and subsequent calls auto-authenticate. CORS tests hit http://localhost:8001 directly (the ingress at the public URL rewrites/strips ACAO headers and makes those checks impossible from outside). reCAPTCHA enforcement: RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY is set in backend/.env so any token sent will hit Google siteverify; invalid tokens reliably return 400. Watch out for stale tests in test_cmgeorges_api.py / test_notifications.py / test_auth_reset_and_ai_drafts.py that still assume reCAPTCHA is disabled.
rca of the issue: No bugs found in the iteration-15 refactor. All four new routers (blog, policies, pricing, discounts) work end-to-end with the same URLs, auth gates, and audit-logging behavior as the pre-refactor monolith. The reCAPTCHA re-enable is correctly enforced on /api/v1/leads and /api/v1/contact with French messages matching the spec. The CORS fix (explicit allow_origins + regex + allow_credentials=True) is verified — allowed origins are reflected, disallowed are not, no wildcards, httpOnly cookies are set on login. The 2 test-file fixes I applied are housekeeping (old tests assumed reCAPTCHA was off); other stale tests in test_cmgeorges_api.py / test_notifications.py have the same root cause and should be updated by the main agent in the same way.
